text:
alice.support: Hey team — ACME reported EU customers are being routed to our us-east edge intermittently since ~09:00 UTC. Symptoms: 1500-2500ms p95, occasional 401s on auth calls, and a spike in billed tokens for the same customer. Can someone triage?

deepa.eng: Can you paste the customer domain + sample client IP and any dig/curl you ran? The 401s could be replay from retries after long lat.

alice.support: Domain: acme-prod.redwood.app. Sample client IP: 88.199.45.12 (ISP: FastNet-EU). Quick dig from customer (sent by them):
```
$ dig +short acme-prod.redwood.app @1.1.1.1
34.200.12.77
```
They showed x-region header coming back as us-east-1 on a curl: `curl -I https://acme-prod.redwood.app` -> `x-rw-region: us-east-1`

bob.sre: That IP is in our us-east pool. Do we have an active anycast region mis-tag? Could be GeoIP DB out-of-date at DNS provider or ISP resolver handing old cache. What are the record TTLs?

alice.support: Our CNAME->regional endpoints TTL is 300s according to config. They reported it persisted for >30m. They ran `dig A @8.8.8.8 acme-prod.redwood.app` and got the same us-east IP. They also did `traceroute` showing hop into us-east cloud provider.

carla.netops: Two quick suspects: 1) DNS provider GeoIP DB rolled back or wrong mapping for that /24; 2) downstream resolver (ISP) has a long cached entry ignoring TTL due to negative caching or operator policy. Also EDNS Client Subnet (ECS) behaviour — if our provider isn't sending ECS, some resolvers will return a suboptimal anycast result.

deepa.eng: Can you run the following from an EU vantage and paste outputs?
```
dig +short @1.1.1.1 acme-prod.redwood.app
dig +short @8.8.8.8 acme-prod.redwood.app
dig +short @resolver1.opendns.com acme-prod.redwood.app
curl -sI https://acme-prod.redwood.app | sed -n '1,20p'
traceroute -n acme-prod.redwood.app
```

alice.support: Pasted results from customer (timestamped):
- @1.1.1.1 -> 34.200.12.77
- @8.8.8.8 -> 34.200.12.77
- opendns -> 34.200.12.77
Headers: `x-rw-region: us-east-1`, `x-rw-node: ue-12`
They also tested from an EU VM (hetzner DE) and initially hit us-east too, then after TTL changes hit eu-west-1.

bob.sre: Sounds like resolver cache affinity across customers. Two parallel action items: (A) Ask DNS provider to confirm GeoIP DB and anycast map hasn't regressed and request a geo-db refresh. (B) For immediate mitigation, raise TTLs low and purge specific records at provider + submit cache flush with major resolvers (Cloudflare/Google/OpenDNS) where supported.

carla.netops: I'll open ticket with DNS provider and include the customer IPs + traceroutes. Also checking whether our regional mapping service returned us-east for that prefix. If provider confirms DB correct, next step is ISP-level caching — we'll need to ask customer to ask their ISP to flush or verify.

alice.support: Customer is asking for repro steps so they can test after we change things. Deepa, can you provide a minimal repro they can run from their side?

deepa.eng: Sure — ask them to run these 4 checks:
1) `dig +short @1.1.1.1 acme-prod.redwood.app` and `dig +short @8.8.8.8 acme-prod.redwood.app` (compare IPs)
2) `curl -I https://acme-prod.redwood.app` and check `x-rw-region` header
3) `curl -v --resolve acme-prod.redwood.app:443:34.200.12.77 https://acme-prod.redwood.app/health` to confirm node responses (if they want to force IP)
4) `traceroute -n acme-prod.redwood.app` to see network path
If both public resolvers return us-east IP while our eu-region mapping shows eu-west-1, capture packet capture of local resolver query if possible.

alice.support: Added as steps to customer. They've asked if this could explain the billing spike — they have retries and long waits leading to duplicate units counted.

bob.sre: Yes, cross-region adds latency causing client-side timeouts -> retries -> duplicate API calls. If auth 401s correlate, it could be that token validation hits a different auth cache in us-east (session key domain) causing intermittent rejection. We'll correlate logs for that customer across regions.

carla.netops: IMHO root cause is likely DNS provider GeoIP mapping + ISP cache. Next steps I will take now: open provider ticket (include sample IPs + timestamps + traceroutes), request immediate geo-db refresh and targeted record purge, and ask provider to set ECS behavior to include client subnet for our records where applicable.

deploy-bot: [deploy] scheduled: config change to lower regional CNAME TTLs to 60s for rollout window (owner: carla.netops). ETA 15m.

alice.support: Thanks. I told ACME we will chase provider and gave repro steps. I'll collect their post-change dig/curl outputs and paste here.

deepa.eng: I'll start log correlation for auth 401 spikes across us-east vs eu-west for that customer id. Assign to me.

bob.sre: If provider response is slow, contingency is to add a weighted routing fallback (prefer eu endpoints for EU ASNs) at our edge DNS map and add a graceful header-based redirect to hint SDKs to prefer eu zone. That is heavier; prefer provider fix first.

alice.support: Customer will try the repro after we push provider purge. Marking P1 for region routing impact. Will update when they post results. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

carla.netops: Provider ticket created #DNS-7421, linked here: https://dnsprovider.example/tickets/7421. Summary: GeoIP mapping mismatch for prefixes 88.199.45.0/24 -> returns us-east IPs. Asked for immediate refresh and cache purge.

alice.support: Updated ACME and waiting on their verification. Thanks all.

carla.netops: Provider responded: performing geo-db refresh and targeted purge now; estimated 10-20m propagation to major resolvers. Will post when done.

alice.support: ACME ran dig again and now gets eu-west IPs. They say p95 latency dropped from 2100ms -> 120ms and no recent 401s. I'll close once stable 30m.

deepa.eng: Confirmed auth 401s correlate with us-east hits; logs look cleaner post-swap. Leaving follow-up task to add monitoring alert for sudden region-shifts per customer (assign deepa).

bob.sre: Nice. Postmortem: if this recurs, need runbook: provider contact template, quick purge steps, and temp routing override. I'll draft runbook.

alice.support: Closing for now; reopen if it reappears. :white_check_mark:
